payload.claim: `retirement_refusal` has no guard for `spec.touches` being empty, unlike the sibling refusal it is explicitly modeled on (`_unmatched_criterion_path`, scheduler.py:291-292, which skips outright when `touches` is empty because that is "the documented shape for a bug awaiting DIAGNOSE", per `intake.py:111-112` and the vocabulary's own definition of Touches: '...by DIAGNOSE on a bug spec, which has none'). Because this refusal runs pre-cell in both `build_queue` and `cli._run_cell`, a `saffron:retired-by` marker that names a bug-type spec (whose `touches` is legitimately `[]` until its own DIAGNOSE phase runs) will refuse that spec permanently before any cell — and therefore before DIAGNOSE — can ever run, with no path to populate `touches` and clear the refusal. This silently recreates, for bug specs, exactly the corpse scenario (`SA-0027`'s whole reason for existing) that the module docstring (scheduler.py:24-32) claims this refusal treats identically to the fifth.
